questions.question: The rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water twice in a day is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tide**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The rhythmic rise and fall of the ocean twice a day is called a **tide.**
 
• The intense **gravitational force** exerted by the sun and the moon on the surface of the earth induce tides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When water covers most of the shore by rising to its maximum level, it is known as **high tide.**
 
• It is** low tide** as the waterfalls to its lowest level and recedes from the sea.
 
• The water of Earth closer to the moon is drawn under the influence of the gravitational force of the moon which creates a high tide.
 
• The sun, the moon, and the earth are in the same line during the full moon and new moon days and the tides are highest. These tides are called the **spring tides**.
 
• But when the moon is in its first and last quarter, the ocean waters are drawn in diagonally opposite directions through the gravitational force of the sun and earth resulting in low tides. These tides are called **neap tides.**
 
• High tides help in navigation as they raise the level of water closer to the coast. This makes it easier for ships to enter the harbour.
 
• High tides assist with fishing as well as much more fish, move closer to the sea during the high tide. This helps fishermen to have an abundant harvest.
 
• The rise and fall of water due to tides is being used in some places to generate electricity.

**Earth's Tides**

 [IMAGE: https://images.theconversation.com/files/244956/original/file-20181111-116841-1euc09g.jpg?ixlib=rb-1.1.0&q=45&auto=format&w=1000&fit=clip]

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a credit rating agency in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RBI.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is India's central bank, **which is responsible for issuing and distributing the Indian rupee and controlling the Indian banking system.**
 
• **It also operates the key payment networks of the nation and works to facilitate its economic growth.** 
 
• RBI began its operations on **1 April 1935** in compliance with the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.**
 
• The RBI was nationalized on **1 January 1949** following India's independence on **15 August 1947.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **credit rating agency** (**CRA,** also referred to as a **rating service)** is a corporation that issues credit ratings that rate the ability of a debtor to pay back loans by making regular payments of principal and interest and the risk of default.
 
• **Credit Review & Research Ltd (CARE)** which started operations in **1993**, is one of India's leading credit rating firm which offers multiple credit scores that help businesses raise money for their diverse needs and help investors make educated investment decisions based on credit risk and their own perceptions of risk-return.
 
• **ICRA** is one of the most experienced credit rating companies in India which rates rupee-denominated loan instruments offered by manufacturing undertakings, commercial banks, non-banking undertakings, public sector undertakings, municipalities and financial institutions.
 
• **CRISIL** Ltd is a global analytical firm offering ratings research and risk and strategy advisory services, and also provides the world's largest banks and major companies with high-end research.

questions.question: Tummalapalle, believed to have one of the largest uranium reserves in the world, is situated in which of the following states?

__
 
• The **Tummalapalle Mine** is a uranium mine located in **Kadapa** in the Indian state of **Andhra Pradesh,** in the **village of Tumalapalli.**
 
• Results from research conducted by **India's Atomic Energy Commission** in 2011 have led analysts to conclude that this mine may have one of the world's largest uranium reserves. 
 
• On 19 July 2011, **Dr. S. Banerjee**, Secretary of the Department of Atomic Energy, who was also Chairman of the Indian Atomic Energy Commission, confirmed reserves of **49,000** **tonnes** and suggested that it could be three times larger to make Tummalapalle the largest uranium deposit mine in the world.
 
• In 2014, the estimates were subsequently raised to **85,000 tonnes.**
 
• Recent findings allegedly show that the reserves are as deep as **1,000 meters.**
 
• This finding has significantly increased India's ability to generate energy from nuclear power plants.
 
• India produced about **3.13 percent** of its energy from nuclear plants as of 2018.
 
• These results indicate that this output can be increased to more than **30 percent** by 2050, which is essential if India hopes to reduce its carbon emissions, pollution, and use.
 
• Not only will this domestic uranium discovery improve India's nuclear energy ambitions, but it will also help cut costs by moving from costly electricity sources like coal.

questions.question: Which of the following scientists was awarded a Nobel Prize for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the Law of the Photoelectric Effect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Albert Einstein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist who founded the theory of relativity, one of the two foundations of scientific physics.**
 
• His work is also known for its influence on scientific theory.
 
• He also discovered the law of** photoelectric effect,** for which he won the Nobel Prize for Physics in **1921.**
 
• The photoelectric effect is a phenomenon in which electrons are released from the surface of the metal when there is a proper light frequency.
 
• **Heinrich Hertz** first documented the idea of the photoelectric effect in 1887, and **Lenard **later in 1902.
 
• Also, Maxwell's electromagnetic wave theory of light couldn't justify both of the results of the photoelectric effect.
 
• Using the groundbreaking theory of Planck that light was a photon, Einstein addressed this question.
 
• The energy that each particle of light carries (called quanta or photon) depends on the frequency of the light (v), as shown: 

**E = hν**

Where** ****h = Planck’s constant = 6.6261 × 10-34 Js.**

 
• **​Because light is bundled into photons, Einstein **theorized that the energy of the whole photon is passed to the electron when a photon falls on the surface of a metal.
 
• Thus, by using the particle nature of light, Einstein demonstrated the Photoelectric effect.

questions.question: A hard disk is an example of which type of data storage device?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Secondary storage**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Secondary storage, also referred to as** auxiliary storage,** is **non-volatile** and is used for later retrieval to store data and programs.
 
• There are several forms of secondary storage, each with benefits and drawbacks.
 
• Either **magnetic **or **optical** storage media are used for most storage systems.
 
• **The hard disk **is an example of secondary storage and magnetic media, which is used for storing data and programs in bulk.
 
• In the case of the computer, they are normally in-built and therefore are not portable.
 
• Some hard drives are reversible, so between machines, they provide easy portable storage.
 
• In general, they are efficient and stable, with easy access to stored data.
 
• This allows the disk to rotate at even greater speeds than it would otherwise do without distorting the disk surface.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the Deputy Governor of Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in January 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Michael Debabrata Patra**__**.**

__
 
• **Michael Patra** is an **economist and central banker from India.**
 
• He is presently a **retired Reserve Bank of India officer, acting as one of its four deputy governors.**
 
• Patra, who joined the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in **1985**, is a career central bank officer.
 
• Patra served as the executive director of the **RBI Monetary Policy** Department prior to his appointment as deputy governor, where he relocated in **2006** and was an internal member of the influential Monetary Policy Committee as well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Earlier, Patra worked in the economic research department of RBI as an advisor in charge of international finance, currency, and banking.
 
• In January 2020, Patra was appointed by the **Cabinet Appointments Committee **as Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India on the advice of the Cabinet Secretary-headed Financial Sector Regulatory Selection Search Committee, replacing **Viral Acharya, **who resigned in July 2019, for a term of **three **years.
 
• Patra became the first RBI career economist to be promoted to the position with his appointment as Deputy Governor.
 
• On **15 January 2020**, Patra took over as Deputy Governor and was appointed to oversee RBI's Department of Monetary Policy, Department of Capital Markets Activities, Department of Financial Markets Supervision, International Department, Department of Economic and Policy Analysis, Department of Statistics and Information Processing, Department of Business Planning and Budget and Financial Stability.
 
• Patra is an ex officio member of the Monetary Policy Committee as the Deputy Governor in charge of the Monetary Policy Branch.

questions.question: ______ is the term used for breeding of fish in specially constructed tanks and ponds.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Pisciculture**__**.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fish farming** or raising the fishes in tanks or ponds is called **Pisciculture. **
 
• The most important species which are being raised worldwide are **Tilapia, Salmon, Carp, and Catfish**.
 
• Pisciculture provides more than **50%** of seafood in the world.
 
• It helps in development by means of generating employment in the fishing community.
 
• Freshwater Cultivable Fishes: **Catla, Rohu, Mrigal, Catfishes, Murrels, and Tilapia**
 
• Marine water cultivable fishes: **Sea bass, Grey mullet, and Milk Fish**
 
• Fishery By-products: **Fish Oil** (comprises of liver and body oil), **Fish meal**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Viticulture:** A branch of Horticulture which deals with the cultivation and harvesting of grapes
 
• **Agriculture**: The science of soil cultivation, crop production, and livestock raising aimed at preparing plant and animal products.
 
• **Horticulture**: Form of agriculture of plants for food and decoration purposes. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea728f908b060e4db8cdc0f37188bd8bacc49aff99cc89b07517095538ec56de.png] 

 
• Pisciculture is a form of **Aquaculture** not of Mariculture.
 
• **Viniculture**: Cultivation and harvesting of grapes specifically for wine production.
 
• Unlike Agriculture, Horticulture does not include large scale crop production and animal husbandry.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is** not** correct?

options.text: The Governor has power to suspend, remit or commute a sentence of death.
The Governor has no power to grant pardon in respect of punishment or sentence inflicted by Court Martial.
The President has the power to grant pardon in respect of punishment or sentence inflicted by Court Martial.
The Governor has the power to grant pardon in case of a death sentence.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Governor has the power to grant a pardon in case of a death sentence**__**.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A Governor is an official who has the power of governing the executive branch of the sub-national level of government i.e. State or Union Territory.
 
• They have similar power and functions as that of the President at the Union level.
 
• In case of a decision granted/announced by the Court of a district/state, the Governor has the power to grant pardon to the accused.
 
• The Governor, as well as the President, has the power to alter the decision announced by the court to grant pardon, suspend, remit, and commute a death sentence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Important Articles related to the Governor:**

 
• Article 155: Appointment
 
• Article 157 and 158: Eligibility of Governor
 
• Article 161: Pardoning power
 
• Article 200: Assent to Bills passed by the state legislature to be amended
 
• Article 201: Bills reserved by Governor for President’s consideration
 
• Article 213: Power to promulgate Ordinance
 
• Article 233: Appointment of District Judges

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b6e4382892525059681a9e234e1123e765e78dea9674deb013b846f94f36971.png] 

 
• The Governor cannot pardon the Death sentence which only can be pardoned by the President.
 
• The Governor has the power to suspend, remit or commute a sentence of death. 
 
• For a pardon, the accused has to file a mercy petition to the Governor or President.

questions.question: In the context of memory size in computer data storage, one gigabyte is equal to how many megabytes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1024 MB**__**.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• One **gigabyte** in the memory context of data storage comprises **1024 MB (megabyte) or 1 million bytes.**
 
• In SI units, it is written as **10⁹**. This is the most commonly used unit of storage in modern times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Unit Conversion Table:**

 
• 4 bit = 1 Nibble
 
• 8 bit = 1 byte
 
• 1 KB (kilobyte) = 1024 byte
 
• 1 MB (megabyte) = 1024 KB
 
• 1 GB (gigabyte) = 1024 MB
 
• 1 TB (terabyte) = 1024 GB
 
• 1 PB (petabyte) = 1024 TB
 
• 1 XB (Exabyte) = 1024 PB
 
• 1 ZB (zettabyte) = 1024 XB
 
• 1 YB (yottabyte) = 1024 ZB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dab57b0ac2c978bda0487de9418f95fbfcd22ac4c4216febd774b8213dc5e3fa.png] 

**Gigabyte** can be explained as –

 
• **Base 10 (Decimal)**: 1 GB = 1000000000 bytes = 1000³ bytes = 10⁹ bytes
 
• बेस 2 (बाइनरी): 1 जीबी = 1073741824 बाइट्स = 10243 बाइट्स = 230 बाइट्स

questions.question: Who among the following scientists invented dynamite?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alfred Nobel**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Swedish scientist,** Alfred Bernhard Nobel** who also founded the Nobel Prize invented Dynamite in **1867.**
 
• Dynamite is based on **Nitro-glycerine** in which wood pulp is used as absorbent and **sodium nitrate** is added to increase the strength of explosive.
 
• **Use of Dynamite:**
 
 
• Construction, Mining, and Demolition
 
• Underwater Blasting
 
 
 
• Dynamite is generally sold as a cylindrical stick that produces **1 Mega Joule** of energy.
 
• The maximum shelf life of Dynamite is **1 year**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Inventions by –**

__
 
• **Thomas Alva Edison**: Bulb, Gramophone, Electric Pen, etc.
 
• **Rudolf Diesel**: Diesel Engine
 
• **Benjamin Franklin:** Lightning rod, Bifocals, Glass Harmonica

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• **Dynamite** and** TNT** (**2, 4, 6 – Trinitrotoluene**) are not the same things.
 
• Earlier, TNT was used as a chemical inside dynamite.
 
• Nitro-glycerine can be detonated easily which is not the case with TNT.
 
• **Chemical Formula –**
 
 
• **Nitro-glycerine**: C₃H₅(ONO₂)­₃
 
• **TNT**: C₇H₅N₃O₆​​

questions.question: The ‘Kathakali’ dance is a harmonious combination of ______ forms of fine art.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Kathakali** is a classical Indian dance form which is a story play genre of art is the folk dance form of **Kerala.**
 
• It is a combination of** 5 forms** of fine art which are –
 
 
• **Natyam (expressions)**
 
• **Nritham (dance)**
 
• **Nrithyam (enactment) **
 
• **Sangeetam (music)**
 
• **Vadya (instruments)**
 
 
 
• Various **costumes** of characters of Kathakali –
 
 
• **Sathwika (Hero)**
 
• **Katti (Villain)**
 
• **Minukku (females)**
 
• **Thathi (other characters)**
 
 
 
• Types of Drums used in Kathakali – **Maddalam, Chenda, and Idakka**
 
• Kathakali is the most difficult style of the traditional dance form in which actors speak ‘sign language’ where hand gestures are used to dictate word part of the character and facial and eye movements express emotions and mood.
 
• **Kathakali **is based on the epics of **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata. ​**

questions.question: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BR Ambedkar**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Dr. Bhim Rao Ambedkar **was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee set up by the Constituent Assembly to prepare a draft of the Constitution of India in** 1947.**
 
• Other members of the Drafting Committee: **Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar**, **N Gopalaswami,** **KM Munshi, Md. Saadulla**, **BL Mitter, DP Khaitan**
 
• Dr. BR Ambedkar is known as the ‘**Father of Constitution of India**’.
 
• Facts about** Constituent Assembly –**
 
 
• **President:** Dr Rajendra Prasad
 
• **Vice President:** Harendra Coomar Mookerjee (later appointed as Governor of West Bengal)
 
• **Constitutional Advisor:** BN Rau (later appointed as Judge in ICJ, The Hague)
 
 
 
• The Constituent Assembly formed **22 **committees of which 10 were on procedural affairs and 12 were on substantive affairs.

questions.question: Which of the following is a disease caused by protozoa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kala Azar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A** chronic and potentially fatal parasitic disease of the viscera (the internal organs, particularly the liver, spleen, bone marrow, and lymph nodes) due to infection by the parasite called Leishmania Donovani.**
 
• The Indian name for this disease is** “black fever,”** which is a reference to the **characteristic darkening of the skin that is seen in patients with this condition**.
 
• **Visceral leishmaniasis (also known as VL or kala-azar)** affects internal organs such as** the liver and spleen. **
 
• It is fatal if not treated.
 
• A **condition called post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (PKDL) may arise six months or more after apparent cure from VL.**

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India has a provision for financial emergency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 360**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 360 of the Constitution of India empowers the president to proclaim a financial emergency on the following ground:

 
 
• If the president is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credibility of India is threatened or in danger.
 
 
 
• The 38th Constitutional Amendment Act 1975 made the satisfaction of the president in declaring a financial emergency final and conclusive.
 
• The satisfaction of the president is held up in any court on any ground.
 
• However 44th Constitutional Amendment Act 1978 deleted this provision.
 
• This means the satisfaction of the president is under Judicial review.
 
• The President may issue directions for the reduction of salaries and allowances to the judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts and of all or any class of persons serving the Union.
 
• Till now, the Financial Emergency has never been invoked in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 356:**** **Article 356 of the Constitution confers a power upon the President to be exercised only where he is satisfied that a situation has arisen where the government of a State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution. Article 356 upon the President is a conditioned power.
 
• **Article 352: **The President can declare such an emergency only on the basis of a written request by the Cabinet headed by the Prime Minister. During a national emergency, many Fundamental Rights of Indian citizens can be suspended.
